title: Scaling Point-in-Time Language Models: Economic Evaluation of Embeddings
claim: Scaling model size and training data closes most of the gap between time-restricted models and unrestricted open-weight baselines.
layout: 1 line plot, time on x-axis, legend at right, horizontal baseline lines
description: A single line chart of HellaSwag accuracy (%) on the y-axis, running from about 20 to 80 and above, against monthly checkpoints over time on the x-axis. The x-axis is cut off in this crop. Two curves with markers rise from left to right. The purple PIT-4B curve, drawn with diamonds, climbs steeply from about 29% and then flattens near 72%. The blue PIT-1.5B curve, drawn with circles, climbs more slowly to about 64%. Thin horizontal lines in different colors mark published baselines: Gemma3-4B at 77% (green), LLaMA-7B at 76% (cyan), Gemma3-1B at 62.3% (orange), DatedGPT at 53.2% (pink), GPT2-XL at 50.9% (red) and ChronoGPT at 44% (brown). A dashed gray line marks random guess at 25%. A boxed legend on the right gives each model's accuracy in bold. The eye goes first to the two rising curves, then to the gap below the top baselines.
caption: HellaSwag accuracy (%) over time for our PIT-1.5B (170B tokens) and PIT-4B (1T tokens) models trained on chronologically ordered FineWeb data. Horizontal lines denote published baselines: Gemma3-4B (77%) [ref], Llama-7B (76%) [ref], GPT2-XL (50.9%) [ref] (as reported in [ref]), Gemma3-1B (62.3%) [ref], ChronoGPT 2024 (44%) [ref], DatedGPT (53.2%) [ref], and random guess (25%).
abstract: Large language models trained on unrestricted internet corpora inevitably embed information from the future, introducing lookahead bias that compromises the validity of backtests and causal inference in finance and the social sciences. Point-in-time language models--trained exclusively on text available up to each calendar date--eliminate this leakage by construction, but existing efforts typically produce models that lag substantially behind their unconstrained counterparts. We show that this performance gap can be substantially narrowed through scale. Training decoder-only transformers with up to 4 billion parameters on 1 trillion chronologically filtered tokens from FineWeb, we construct a sequence of monthly model checkpoints spanning 2013-2024. Across a range of common-sense reasoning and language understanding benchmarks, our models approach the performance of leading open-weight models of comparable size (e.g., Gemma-3-4B and LLaMA-7B) trained on temporally unrestricted data, although a performance gap remains on several tasks. Instruction fine-tuning via LoRA further improves downstream usability. We release the complete pipeline--including dataset construction, training infrastructure, and evaluation code--to enable reproducible point-in-time language modeling and to support research applications that require strict temporal validity.
